nodes.name: perception_3d
nodes.description: Represent common 3D perception preprocessing and spatial verification primitives.
nodes.conceptual_summary: 3D perception pipelines build point voxels, fuse image evidence, draw ego-centric BEV rasters, and verify image correspondences.
nodes.critic_notes: Model inference, learned feature extraction, GPU kernels, and dataset-specific metadata loading are outside this atom family.
nodes.decomposition_rationale: The research packet identified four separable deterministic primitives used across 3D detection, motion forecasting, and image retrieval solutions.

nodes.name: voxelize_point_cloud
nodes.description: Assign point-cloud rows to fixed xyz voxels with capped per-voxel storage.

inputs.name: points
inputs.constraints: Finite N x D array with at least xyz columns.

inputs.name: voxel_size
inputs.constraints: Positive voxel widths for x, y, z.

inputs.name: point_range
inputs.type_desc: tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float]
inputs.constraints: xyz minimum bounds followed by larger xyz maximum bounds.

inputs.name: max_points_per_voxel
inputs.constraints: Positive cap on stored points per voxel.

outputs.name: result
outputs.constraints: Voxel features, voxel xyz coordinates, and saturated point counts.

nodes.type_signature: (points: NDArray[np.floating], voxel_size: tuple[float, float, float], point_range: tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float], max_points_per_voxel: int) -> tuple[NDArray[np.floating], NDArray[np.int64], NDArray[np.int64]]
nodes.conceptual_summary: Convert unordered point rows into fixed-size voxel buckets for sparse 3D detection backbones.
nodes.critic_notes: This CPU atom does not implement GPU scatter kernels, dynamic voxelization, or learned voxel feature encoders.
nodes.decomposition_rationale: Voxelization is a preprocessing boundary reused by LiDAR detectors before learned feature extraction.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Bins N points into a 3D grid, finding occupied voxels and populating at most M points per voxel for V active voxels in linear time, requiring O(V * M * D) space for voxel features and O(N) space for voxel assignments (derived from analyzing the actual function hard voxelization rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.name: project_image_to_points
nodes.description: Project 3D points into a camera feature map and append bilinear samples.

inputs.name: points_3d
inputs.constraints: Finite N x D array with at least xyz columns.

inputs.name: image_features
inputs.constraints: Finite H x W x C image feature tensor.

outputs.name: result
outputs.constraints: N rows with original point columns plus sampled image channels.

nodes.type_signature: (points_3d: NDArray[np.floating], image_features: NDArray[np.floating], intrinsic: NDArray[np.floating], extrinsic: NDArray[np.floating], image_shape: tuple[int, int]) -> NDArray[np.floating]
nodes.conceptual_summary: Fuse 2D image evidence into 3D point rows through camera projection and interpolation.
nodes.critic_notes: Camera calibration selection, occlusion handling, and neural image feature computation are outside this atom.
nodes.decomposition_rationale: Projection and bilinear feature lookup are deterministic geometry pieces of multi-modal LiDAR-camera fusion.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Transforms and projects N 3D coordinates using extrinsic/intrinsic matrices in O(N) time and samples C-dimensional features via bilinear interpolation in O(N * C) time, requiring O(N * C) auxiliary space for the output (derived from analyzing the actual function point painting projection rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.name: rasterize_bev
nodes.description: Draw agent trajectories and static map polylines into a two-channel ego-centric BEV raster.

inputs.name: agents
inputs.constraints: Finite A x T x K tensor with xy coordinates in the first two columns.

outputs.name: result
outputs.constraints: Binary tensor with shape 2 x H x W.

nodes.type_signature: (agents: NDArray[np.floating], map_elements: Sequence[NDArray[np.floating]], ego_pose: NDArray[np.floating], raster_size: tuple[int, int], resolution: float) -> NDArray[np.uint8]
nodes.conceptual_summary: Convert vector scene context into image-like BEV channels for motion models.
nodes.critic_notes: This atom omits semantic color palettes, map API calls, and history/future channel expansion.
nodes.decomposition_rationale: Rasterization is a deterministic data assembly step distinct from learned motion forecasting.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Initializes a 2-channel raster grid of shape H x W and projects/draws N trajectory and polyline coordinate segments using a step-based line-drawing algorithm in O(N + H * W) time and O(H * W) auxiliary space (derived from analyzing the actual function BEV rasterization rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.name: ransac_homography
nodes.description: Estimate a homography from noisy point correspondences with RANSAC inlier selection.

inputs.name: src_points
inputs.constraints: Finite N x 2 source coordinates with N >= 4.

inputs.name: dst_points
inputs.constraints: Finite N x 2 destination coordinates paired with src_points.

outputs.name: result
outputs.constraints: 3x3 homography matrix and length-N inlier mask.

nodes.type_signature: (src_points: NDArray[np.floating], dst_points: NDArray[np.floating], threshold: float, max_iterations: int, seed: int = 0) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.bool_]]
nodes.conceptual_summary: Reject bad feature matches by fitting a planar projective transform and scoring reprojection error.
nodes.critic_notes: Feature detection, descriptor matching, and bundle adjustment are outside this atom.
nodes.decomposition_rationale: Spatial verification is a reusable geometry primitive in image retrieval and matching pipelines.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Runs I RANSAC iterations where each iteration fits a homography on a 4-point sample in O(1) time and evaluates reprojection errors on all N points in O(N) time, followed by a final DLT refit on the best inlier set in O(N) time, requiring O(N) auxiliary space (derived from analyzing the actual function DLT homography with RANSAC rather than the opaque wrapper)
